body:
Good Thursday morning, Bakersfield. The story leading the day is a police standoff at a northwest apartment complex that stretched past 2 a.m., with residents led out through a back garage door and an entry team moving in from the rear. Closer to home, Dolores Huerta is on many minds after Wednesday night's candlelight vigil downtown. Outside it's 55 degrees at Meadows Field, headed for a high near 72 under no active weather alerts, with air quality sitting at a moderate 79.

## The Kern Overnight

The night's biggest call came at 1:55 a.m., when officers worked an apartment complex in northwest Bakersfield through the early hours. Residents of several units were brought out through a garage door at the rear of the building while an armored vehicle was moved into position out front and the entry team came in from the back. Once inside, officers found bullet holes in the doorway of an upstairs unit. No further details were available by morning.

Shots were reported twice in quick succession at 4:33 a.m., both in northwest Bakersfield. The first call described six to eight rounds in the 10800 block of Royal Ascot Avenue; the second, about 12 rounds in the 10000 block of Laurel Park Avenue. Officers had no additional information on either report.

Earlier in the evening, at 7:17 p.m., officers were sent to a mobile home park for a 15-year-old in a white shirt and black pants reported to be holding a gray handgun. At 9:08 p.m., a driver on northbound Interstate 5 north of Fort Tejon flagged down an officer and said a man had tried to force him out of his vehicle and take his keys and wallet.

The Grapevine kept crews busy late. At 9:58 p.m., a semi rear-ended another semi on northbound Interstate 5 half a mile south of the Grapevine, pinning one driver inside the tractor-trailer. Firefighters freed him, and crews asked for a hard closure of the lanes. The log also included a 7:00 p.m. call to the 2500 block of Taft Highway for a man reported lying on the sidewalk in front of a business, a 7:09 p.m. verbal disturbance at a phone store in the 10300 block of Main Street that drew two callers, and a 7:22 p.m. welfare check on Hermosa Drive in east Bakersfield, where a man told officers his roommates were pressuring him to take hospital-prescribed medicine or move out.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 72 degrees today and a low around 56 tonight, according to the National Weather Service. It's currently 55 degrees at Meadows Field. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and no active fires reported in the area. Air quality is running at 79, which lands in the moderate range — fine for most of us, though if you're sensitive to smoke or dust, it's a reasonable day to keep an eye on how you feel during longer stretches outside. Otherwise, it's a quiet, mild late-October day in the valley, the kind that makes the walk from the car to the office an easy one.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that king tides have inundated parts of both U.S. coasts, flooding streets and pushing seawater into homes and businesses in beach communities across California, Florida and the Carolinas.** The tides began with the full moon earlier this week and could keep causing flooding in some areas into the weekend, forecasters said. Along the California coast, a super El Niño has warmed the ocean and raised the volume of seawater, and Kelvin waves — pulses of warm water that lift sea level — are adding to it, according to Roger Gass, a meteorologist with the weather service's Bay Area office in Monterey. In Southern California, officials shut down traffic on a flooded stretch of the Pacific Coast Highway. It's a coastal story, but a useful reminder for anyone headed over the hill this weekend to check conditions before the drive.

**According to 23ABC, a candlelight vigil Wednesday night honored the late labor leader Dolores Huerta near the site of the future Dolores Huerta Peace and Justice Cultural Center in downtown Bakersfield.** The ceremony drew dozens of residents and community leaders, along with members of Huerta's family. Her daughter Lori de Leon remembered her mother as fearless in pushing for better treatment of farmworkers, knocking on doors and talking to legislators even as a young single mother. Lisa Buckner, who was mentored by Huerta as a young activist in the 1970s, said the size of the crowd was a testament to how many lives she touched. Huerta's son Emilio also spoke, echoing his sister's words about their mother's tenacity and asking those gathered to think fondly of her.

**KGET 17 reports that the political world is reacting to Huerta's death, with tributes coming in from leaders across California and beyond.** The station's coverage reflects how widely her influence reached — from the fields of the San Joaquin Valley to state and national politics. For Kern County, the loss lands close to home: Huerta's organizing work began here, and the cultural center rising downtown will carry her name.

**KGET 17 also reports that work continues on the Dolores Huerta Cultural Center, even as the project's inspiration has passed.** The center is planned for downtown Bakersfield, and Wednesday's vigil was held near the future site. Organizers have described it as a place meant to carry forward Huerta's legacy of community organizing and justice work. There's no word yet on a completion date, but the project remains in motion.

**23ABC reports that the Arvin City Council is weighing a commercial cannabis storage and processing facility that supporters say could bring new jobs to the city.** Leef Arvin LLC has applied for a site development permit, a commercial cannabis permit and a development agreement for a facility at 818 South Derby Street, where an existing warehouse and cold storage building would be converted and 12 large storage containers added. Consultant planner Isaiah Medina told the city the project would start with about 12 full-time jobs and could add 16 seasonal part-time workers during harvest. Hirsh Jain of Ananda Strategy said cannabis stored in Arvin would be trucked to Willits, in far Northern California, to be extracted into oils used by major California cannabis brands. The council has not yet decided.

**KGET 17 reports that another judge has rejected the Department of Justice's fight over a California ballot measure.** Details of the ruling were not immediately available, but the decision is another turn in the ongoing legal back-and-forth between federal officials and the state over election rules. We'll follow it as more comes out.

**Bakersfield Now reports that The Patch is back for another year of fall fun and Halloween excitement.** The seasonal attraction returns with its usual lineup of pumpkin-themed activities and family-friendly scares. If you're still sorting out weekend plans with the kids, it's worth a look before Halloween arrives Saturday.

## Something good

Shafter's Dual Immersion program is showing what bilingualism looks like in practice, with students in the community learning in two languages side by side. Programs like this one give kids a skill they'll carry for life — and they're a point of pride for a town that knows how to make things grow. If you know a student in the program, give them a high five this week.

## Coming up this week

Halloween lands on Saturday, and there's plenty on the calendar before and after. At the Fox Theater, Elias Medina takes the stage Friday, October 30. Journey USA plays the Fox on Saturday, November 7, with Texas Tornado Tradition also on the bill that day, and the Cults & Classics series continues with a screening of "Play Misty for Me" on Monday, November 9. NUTCRACKER! Magical Christmas Ballet arrives November 13, and season passes for the 2026–2027 Cults & Classics lineup are already on sale.

On the civic side, the Bakersfield City Council meets twice on Wednesday, November 4 — first at 3:30 p.m. and again at 5:15 p.m. The Planning Commission meets Thursday, November 5 at 5:30 p.m. If the Arvin cannabis proposal is on your radar, keep an eye on that city's agenda as well; the council there is still weighing the Leef Arvin application. And if you're headed to the coast this weekend, check the tide and road conditions before you go — the king tides are expected to linger into the weekend.

top.title: King tides inundate streets and flood homes and businesses along both US coasts
